title: The recorded M4+ share rose 2.63 times in an Oklahoma box after disposal cuts, but seven late events limit the evidence
abstract: We test whether the decline after disposal cuts has the same size distribution in a broad Oklahoma box. ComCat has 66 M4+ events among 2,111 M3+ events in 2014-2016 and seven among 85 in 2021-2025. The share ratio is 2.63. A half-degree spatial adjustment gives an odds ratio of 2.33. Removing 2024 leaves four late M4+ events and an independent-event interval that includes no change. A discrete Gutenberg-Richter fit above M2.5 predicts 160 peak M4+ events against 66 recorded. When scaled by the observed late M2.5+ count, it predicts 7.61 late M4+ events against seven; the peak empirical size mix predicts 3.13. Thus agreement with the late count can hide poor peak size calibration. Preferred magnitude types have strong size selection. These exploratory results constrain recorded size calibration but do not identify the residual driver or explain short clustering. We provide code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Recorded size fractions, annual counts and year-block resampling. Dashed size curves are single-slope discrete Gutenberg-Richter fits. Seven late M4+ events and magnitude-type selection limit physical interpretation.
